No year, because the two starting amounts differ even though the rates differ
options.misconception: believes matching starting amounts decide whether two lines meet

options.text: Every year, because both clubs add members to their base in every row
options.misconception: confuses a shared trend with a shared value

options.text: Two years, one where the gap closes and one where it opens again
options.misconception: expects two crossings from a pair of straight lines

questions.explanation: Setting 6y plus 40 equal to 4y plus 58 gives 2y equals 18, so y equals 9. Two lines with different rates cross at most once, and here they do cross, so the count is exactly one.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.topic: Graph of a linear equation in two variables
questions.learningObjective: explain how a table of values determines the graph of a linear equation
questions.stem: A library circulation table lists, for a reading club, the rule 2x plus 3y equals 12 with the two rows 0,4 and 3,2. Explain how the table shows the shape of the graph of that equation.

answer.exemplar: Every row of the table satisfies the equation, so each row marks a point that lies on the graph. The rows 0,4 and 3,2 both check out, and because the equation is linear its graph is a single straight line, so those two points determine its direction. Any point of the line can be found by choosing x, solving for y, and that value of y is the height the graph has at that x. The trap is to treat the table as a list of separate answers rather than as points that must fit one straight line.

questions.explanation: The rows 0,4 and 3,2 both satisfy 2x plus 3y equals 12, so they are points on the graph. Because the equation is linear, those points lie on one straight line, and every other solution plots on that same line.
questions.hint: Check each row against the equation before plotting.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.learningObjective: find a rate of change from two rows of a table
questions.stem: A rowing club table lists two splits, 500 metres in 82 seconds and 1500 metres in 251 seconds. Explain how to find the rate of change in seconds per 500 metres from these two rows.

answer.exemplar: The two rows give a point each, with the distance in units of 500 metres and the time in seconds: 1 and 82, then 3 and 251. The rate of change is the change in time divided by the change in distance, so 251 minus 82 equals 169 seconds over 3 minus 1 equals 2 steps, giving 84.5 seconds for each 500 metres. Averages and raw differences do not work here, because the two rows are not adjacent in the table, so the 169 seconds cover two 500 metre steps rather than one.

questions.explanation: Treat each row as a point, then divide the change in time, 169 seconds, by the change in distance, 2 steps of 500 metres, to get 84.5 seconds per step. Using 251 minus 82 without dividing by 2 would double the rate.
questions.hint: Rise over run, using the change across the two rows.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.learningObjective: explain the product test for perpendicular slopes
questions.stem: A joinery table records two rails: Rail 1 climbs 3 centimetres for every 1 centimetre of run, and Rail 2 drops 1 centimetre for every 3 centimetres of run. Explain why these two rails meet at a right angle.

answer.exemplar: Rail 1 has a slope of 3, since it climbs 3 for every 1 of run, and Rail 2 has a slope of negative one third, since it drops 1 for every 3 of run. The two slopes are negative reciprocals, and their product is negative one, which is the test for perpendicular lines. Slopes of opposite sign alone are not enough, because a line of slope negative 2 and a line of slope negative one half are parallel rather than perpendicular, so the sizes of the slopes matter as well as the signs.

questions.explanation: The slopes are 3 and negative one third, and their product is negative one, which is the condition for perpendicular lines. Opposite signs alone are not enough, since a pair of negative slopes can still be parallel.
questions.hint: Multiply the two slopes and check for negative one.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.learningObjective: convert a rule into standard form and explain the steps
questions.stem: A district table of school runs gives the rule y equals negative 2 x plus 6 for one bus route. Explain how to write this rule in standard form with both variables on the left.

answer.exemplar: Standard form places the x term first, then the y term, then the constant, so the rule becomes 2x plus y equals 6. Starting from y equals negative 2 x plus 6, add 2x to both sides to get 2x plus y equals 6, and no term is left on the right. The sign of the x coefficient flips because it moved to the other side of the equals sign, and a rule that is already written with the variables on the left needs no rearrangement at all.

questions.explanation: Adding 2x to both sides of y equals negative 2x plus 6 gives 2x plus y equals 6, which is standard form. Moving the x term across flips its sign, and the constant stays on the right.
questions.hint: Move the x term across and keep the constant on the right.

questions.stem: A warehouse table lists three shelves at aisle 4 with bays 2, 6 and 10, and the staff note that the aisle never changes. Explain why the slope of the line through these points cannot be given as a number.

answer.exemplar: Each of the three points has the same first coordinate, 4, so the line through them is vertical. The slope formula divides the change in the second coordinate by the change in the first, and here the change in the first is 0 between any two rows. A rise of 4, 4 or 4 over a run of 0 cannot be evaluated, so the slope is undefined rather than zero. It is the one direction in the plane for which a rate of change does not exist, which is why it is treated separately whenever slopes are compared.

questions.explanation: The first coordinate is 4 in every row, so the run between any two points is 0 and the rise over zero cannot be computed. A vertical line has no rate of change, so its slope is undefined instead of zero.
questions.hint: Check what the denominator of the slope formula becomes.

questions.explanation: Subtracting 4x gives 2y equals 18 minus 4x, and dividing by 2 gives y equals negative 2x plus 9, so the intercept is 9. The constant must be divided by 2 as well, or the rule changes shape.
questions.hint: Divide every term by 2, not just the variable terms.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.learningObjective: diagnose a sign error made when converting to standard form
questions.stem: A table of savings plans gives the rule y equals 5x plus 8, and a student writes it in standard form as 5x plus y equals negative 8. What is the error?

options.text: Both variable terms need a negative sign, giving negative 5x plus y equals negative 8
options.misconception: negates both variable terms at once

options.text: Nothing is wrong, because any arrangement of the same terms is equivalent
options.misconception: believes any arrangement of the terms is equivalent

options.text: The y term must be subtracted, so the correct form is 5x minus y equals negative 8
The constant belongs on the left, giving 5x plus y plus 8 equals 0
options.misconception: leaves the y term positive on the wrong side

questions.explanation: Moving y across the equals sign turns it into negative y, so the standard form is 5x minus y equals negative 8. The sign of the y term is what changes when it crosses, and leaving it positive reverses the rule.
questions.hint: Watch the sign of the term that moves across.
